prompt:
A rigid gas storage cylinder of volume 0.0400 m^3 is filled with nitrogen gas (N_2, molar mass 28.0 g mol^-1) at an initial pressure of 5.20 * 10^6 Pa and a temperature of 22.0 °C.
Take R = 8.31 J K^-1 mol^-1 and N_A = 6.02 * 10^23 mol^-1.
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Diagram of a heavy steel gas cylinder of volume 0.0400 m^3 with pressure gauge reading 5.20 MPa. A valve releases nitrogen gas slowly over 4.00 hours, after which the pressure drops to 3.50 MPa at 17.0 °C.]
(a) Show that the initial amount of nitrogen gas in the cylinder is approximately 85 mol. [2]
(b) Over a period of 4.00 hours, nitrogen gas escapes slowly through a faulty valve into the atmosphere. At the end of the 4.00 hours, the pressure inside the cylinder has decreased to 3.50 * 10^6 Pa and its temperature is 17.0 °C.
  (i) Calculate the amount of nitrogen gas remaining in the cylinder. [2]
  (ii) Calculate the mass of nitrogen gas that has escaped, in kilograms. [2]
(c) Calculate the average rate at which nitrogen molecules escaped from the cylinder, in molecules per second. [1]

parts.description: Show initial moles is approx 85 mol
Calculate mass of gas escaped in kg

part_enrichment.guidance: Award M1 for converting 22.0 °C to 295.15 K and substituting into n = pV / (RT). Award A1 for showing 84.8 mol before stating approximately 85 mol.
part_enrichment.common_pitfalls: Omitting the unrounded calculation (84.8 mol) in a 'show that' question.

part_enrichment.guidance: Award M1 for converting 17.0 °C to 290.15 K and substituting into n = pV / (RT). Award A1 for 58.1 mol.
part_enrichment.common_pitfalls: Using the initial temperature 22.0 °C instead of the new temperature 17.0 °C.

part_enrichment.guidance: Award M1 for subtracting moles (84.8 - 58.1 = 26.7 mol) and multiplying by molar mass M in kg mol^-1 (0.0280 kg mol^-1). Award A1 for 0.749 kg.
part_enrichment.common_pitfalls: Leaving the mass in grams (749 g) when the question specifies kilograms.

part_enrichment.guidance: Award A1 for multiplying moles lost by N_A and dividing by time in seconds (4.00 * 3600 = 14400 s) to get 1.12 * 10^21 molecules s^-1.
part_enrichment.common_pitfalls: Dividing by 4.00 hours directly instead of converting to seconds.

answer:
(a) n_1 = 84.8 mol approx 85 mol
(b)(i) 58.1 mol
(b)(ii) 0.749 kg
(c) 1.12 * 10^21 molecules s^-1

mark_scheme.criterion: (a) Obtains n_1 = 84.8 mol (must show at least 3 s.f. before rounding to 85 mol)
(b)(ii) Calculates Delta n = 84.805 - 58.064 = 26.74 mol and multiplies by M = 0.0280 kg mol^-1
(b)(ii) Delta m = 0.749 kg (allow 0.748 kg to 0.750 kg)

hints: In (a), convert 22.0 °C to kelvin and calculate n = pV / (RT).
In (b)(i), use the new pressure 3.50 * 10^6 Pa and new temperature 17.0 °C (290.15 K).
In (b)(ii), subtract remaining moles from initial moles and multiply by molar mass in kg mol^-1.
In (c), find total molecules lost using Delta N = Delta n * N_A and divide by total time in seconds.
teacher_walkthrough: Synthesizes cylinder thermodynamics, non-isothermal leak dynamics, mass loss, and particle escape rate.
Remind students to track time in seconds when evaluating rates in s^-1.
